content.text:
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
Results. Operating cash flow ratio was 112% for Q1 2023, compared to 113% in Q1 2022. Adjusted net income for Q1 2023 was BRL 167 million, in line with the same period from the previous year, mainly due to the higher financial expenses related to UNIT and FITS acquisitions and higher interest rates. Our adjusted EPS for the quarter reached BRL 1.77, the same when compared to Q1 2022. Our EPS performance reflected the decrease in our net income that was compensated by capital allocation discipline executing buyback programs. Moving to slide number nine for discussions of key operational metrics by business unit.
Our number of medical students grew 19% over Q1 2023, reaching 20,800 students, with operating medical seats increasing 25% due to the encompass of 632 medical seats related to Mais Médicos and Ji-Paraná, Itabuna seats increase, UNIT Alagoas, and FITS Jaboatão acquisitions, as previously said. Therefore, we reached 3,163 approved seats and expect to achieve almost 23,000 undergrad medical students at maturity. Our net average tickets, excluding acquisitions, increased by 8.3% over the same period last year, reaching BRL 8,570 in Q1 2023, compared to BRL 7,861 in Q1 2022. The last graph shows a 24% growth in combined tuition fees, reaching BRL 806 million, up from BRL 649 million from Q1 2022, 78% of which are related to medicine courses.
All these efforts means one thing: our medical educational business remains and will continue to be the cornerstone of our business in the short and the middle terms, delivering high predictable growth combined with solid profitability and cash generation. On the next page, I will present our continual educational metrics. As said before, we saw another year of great recovery in our continual educational segments, with an increase of more than 37% in the number of students compared to the same quarter last year, reaching 4,774 students. In addition, for the quarter, net revenues grew 47% when compared to Q1 2022. This recovery is mainly due to the robust intake process and course maturation. Moving to slide number 11, I will discuss the digital service operational metrics.
On the first graph, you can see our total active payers, which are the ones that generate revenues in business to physicians, B2P. With a continuous growth trend, we've reached 218,000 paying users, a 24% growth compared to the same period last year. As you can see in the second graph, our ecosystem grew 13.6% compared to the previous year, achieving 295,000 monthly active users, representing almost 40% of all medical students and physicians in Brazil. Finally, on our last graph, we can see our digital service net revenues, which increased more than 19% when compared to the same quarter of the last year, reaching BRL 56.8 million.
With the breakdown our digital service net revenue within B2P and B2B segments, which accounted for more than BRL 46 million coming from B2P and more than BRL 10 million coming from B2B, since B2B strategy is still ramping up, representing a growth of 62% compared to the prior year. Now moving to my three last slides, I will discuss our cash and net debt positions, also giving more color on our cost of debt. Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the Q1 were BRL 723 million, a decrease of 8% over March 2022, and 34% when compared to the Q4 2022. Mainly to the new debentures issues during the Q4 that was used to fund the down payment of UNIT Alagoas and FITS Jaboatão acquisitions in January. On the next page, we can look closely to the net debt variation.
In Q1 2023, net debt totaled BRL 2,029,000,000, an increase of BRL 648 million when compared to Q4 2022, mainly to the BRL 825 million UNIT Alagoas and FITS Jaboatão acquisitions, which was partially offset by BRL 177 million of free cash flow generation in Q1 2023. On the next slide, you can see a table with the breakdown of our gross debts and the total cost of our debts, considering our main source of debts, the SoftBank transactions, debentures, accounts payables to selling shareholders, and other financial obligations. This ends our prepared remarks. Strong performance, consistent growth and success in all segments. We are committed to provide an ecosystem that integrates educational and digital solutions for the entire medical journey, enhancing the development, updating, assertiveness, and productivity of health professionals.
We are very proud of our business and what we have achieved so far, and excited about what we plan for the future. I will now open the conference for Q&A session. Thank you.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
If you want to ask a question, please raise your hand. The first question comes from Lucca Marquezini from Itaú BBA. Lucca, you may talk.
Lucca Marquezini
Analyst, Itau BBA
Good evening, everyone, and thank you for taking our question. Regarding Medcel, we've seen a decrease in the number of active payers for the past quarters. Can you please provide more color on the competitive landscape and comment if you have seen any sign of recovery here, especially considering the initiatives implemented in the end of last year. That would be helpful, please. Thank you.
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
Hi, Lucca. This is Virgilio. I can start here. Blanco can give more details after. Just about the dynamic on Medcel. We are combining the Medcel offering on pillar one together with Além da Medicina and Afya Papers. We are seeing a very good intake enrollments coming on Além da Medicina and Afya Papers, also shifting demand between these offerings in the pillar one. Medcel, as we saw in the last quarter, on Q4, we still have a lower volume coming this year. We are ending the seasonality right now in Q1. The next cycle, the big cycle start in September. We still have for this semester, a lower number coming from Medcel when you compare to last year. The competition landscape is still have the same.
We still have a lot of competitors on this matter. That's the reason why we changed not only the product, but also changed the offering combining Além da Medicina and Afya Papers, offering much more related also for specialization. It's much more online continuum medical education than only residency prep course as it used to be Medcel in the past back in 2019, 2018. Just to give more figures, I pass back to Blanco that can color a little bit about the numbers. Thank you. Thanks, Virgilio. Lucca, as Virgilio mentions, we end at the Q1 the intake of the collections of 2023. All the collection of 2022 is disconnected during this quarter. Now the new intake will take place in the Q4. Medcel, as we mentioned, is not a cornerstone for our business-to-business strategy.
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
We still feel comfortable that with this combined offer that we are doing with the prep task of Medcel within Afya Papers and Além da Medicina contents we're going to stop this following of Medcel, and then we can have some kind of recover during the next intake cycle for the 2024 collections that we are going to start on September.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Yeah. Virgilio, you want to complement?
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
Yeah, just to add a point here. Moving forward for the following quarters on the digital, and as the next quarter will be consolidated, it'll be fully organic when you compare to the previous year. Pillar one should be moving around 10% to 15% above last year, and the other components of our digital services should be growing close above 30%. The combination of them will be around something 15% to 20% for the rest of the year, at least for the rest of the H1 because we still have the intake that will be stronger on the H2. Okay?
Lucca Marquezini
Analyst, Itau BBA
That's very clear. Thank you, Virgilio and Luis.
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
Thank you.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Okay, our next question comes from Mauricio Cepeda from Credit Suisse. Mauricio, you may go.
Maurício Cepeda
Analyst, Credit Suisse
Hi, Virgilio, Blanco, Renata. Thank you for the space here. A little bit on margins. I understand that you are, in fact, reconfiguring the mix of business there. We see that the margins are being a little bit lower, but for a very positive reason, right? You're ramping up a lot continuous education. You're opening lots of medical seats. My first question would be, how do you expect this to go on for this year in terms of these apparent margin pressures which are, in fact, the success of the businesses? Thinking a little bit more further, when you see basically a convergence to, let's say, a new margin level, given that you're integrating new operations on top of the mentioned effects. Thank you.
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
Mauricio Cepeda, it's Blanco speaking. Regarding the expectations in the year, we are fully committed for what we have guided for the market with the disclosure of the results of 2022. The margins embedded in our guidance is between 40% to 42%, from the bottom to the top line of the guidance. We are committed with that. Remember that Q1 is the best quarter that we always have due to the seasonality of our business. We have this a little bit pressure in these margins caused by Medcel performance, the four new Med schools, and for the beginning of UNIT that is coming with margins that were initially better than expected in the original business plan, but still behind the margins of the integrated companies. If we exclude these acquisitions for 2023, the decreasing margins is just 50 bps.
We are pretty committed to deliver the margins of this 40% to 42%. As you mentioned, as continuing education will grow and the digital segments will grow with higher rates than the undergrad segments, we're going to have some kind of shifts for margins. For this year, the guidance is between 40% to 42%.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Yes, Cepeda, we unfortunately do not give guidance for longer term. There is no reason for margins with all the segments to increase in the following years. Virgilio, do you want to complement?
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
I think just as we are growing very fast in continuing medical education in PEBMED, we launched six new campuses. We are preparing to launch another two or three campuses still this year. As any other on-ground operation for education, we will ramp up the number of students per campuses. Gross margin will increase and also EBITDA margin will increase along the year. We expect to have better contribution margin coming from continuing medical education for the following semester, not only for the legacy operation, but also mainly for the new campuses that we launched last year and also this year. Okay.
Maurício Cepeda
Analyst, Credit Suisse
That's very clear. Thank you.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Just a reminder, if you want to ask a question, just raise your hand. The next question will come from Lucas Nagano from Morgan Stanley. Lucas, you may now talk.
Lucas Nagano
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Hey, good evening, y'all. Thanks for taking our questions. I have two. The first one is related to your med schools. The situation seems still very comfortable. You increased prices 8%, filled 100% of seats. Have you noticed any underlying change in the demand? For example, how it evolved in the Southeast versus the med schools in terms of candidates per seat or pricing, for example. The second question is related to B2B. It seems to be performing well. Can you tell us a little which part of the product development process and the commercialization process you are in? Also, if you could comment a little if you're developing solutions for companies that are not in the pharma industry.
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
Yes, Lucas, I can take the first one here. Blanco helped me on the second one. About the tuition adjustment, that was the average across the board. About intake level this year was, when you compare to the last four years, was the candidate per seat ratio higher than the highest ratio candidate per seat that we had for the last four years. We are reaching around eight candidates per seat. Of course, this is on a national average. As we have a very integrated process, we can manage to have 100% of occupancy in all of our units. Of course, that we have different ratio between our campuses. When we analyze our campuses in large cities like Universidade Unigranrio in Rio de Janeiro, we have more than 20, 25 candidates per seat.
For some institution have around four and five candidates per seat, but it's pretty feasible and easy to keep enrolling 100% of the seats every semester. Even considering that we are passing tuition a little bit above inflation this semester, I think we are strengthening our commercial process, our enrolling process, and our capacity to convert students to all of our campuses.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
If I may add a point here, I just want to mention that we do have different prices in different regions, and that's mainly because of the regions. That does not mean that we have different margins in different regions, because all the costs and expenses related to different regions are also different. What I'm trying to say here, at the end of the day, that tickets from our medical school, comparing to, I don't know, Unigranrio is different. In the end of the day, we can see similar margins. What changed the margin level is mostly how much concentrated the school is from Afya. That's what changed the game. Blanco, may you take the second question?
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
Yeah. Lucas, thank you for your questions. Just give you more color on the B2B. I just give a step back to give more color in our strategy. Our digital strategy is focused on penetrating within the physicians with the best solutions to increase their productivity, to increase their assertiveness, and to increase their updating from topics. We've been these channels to connect these physicians to the healthcare players. We divided the digital in these two parts. Okay, regarding the companies that we provide this service for the physicians, we are increasing a lot the users, the monthly active users, and we increasing the players as well.
Regarding the B2B, what we had in place until right now is the connections that we've made in a minor part with other educational companies to provide solutions such as our prep course, Medcel, and our medicine image solutions, that is Medical Harbour. Most part of these digital revenues are coming from the pharmaceutical industry. We have more than 100 contracts established till now, with more than 40 pharmaceutical industry players right now, multinationals and national players on that. All the B2B revenues are coming from these two parts. What we have launched right now, we started the connections for the second pillar of the industry that it's relevant for our B2B strategy. That is the providers. We just are getting up a team to do these connections and starting to offer our connections with the physicians to the providers.
In the pharmaceutical industry, what we are providing right now, it's what the industry call as e-detailing. That is marketing and commercial efforts to connect the physicians with the industry players to get their latest drugs.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Treatments
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
treatments for the physicians. For providers, we are going to offer recruitment service and offering the best leads that can come from our ecosystem, leads for them to get their treatment. Buying some medicine, doing their treatments or doing the assessments. That's the strategy, Lucas.
Lucas Nagano
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Very clear, Virgilio, Blanco, and Renata. Thank you very much.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
Of course. Just a reminder, if you want to ask a question, please just raise your hand. The next question comes from Jessica from JPMorgan. Jessica, you may now go.
Jessica Mehler
Analyst, JPMorgan
Hi. Thank you for taking my questions. I have two. First, how are medicine tickets expected to behave going forward? Do you expect to increase prices above inflation? This is the second question. Do you have any updates regarding the new Mais Médicos program? Thank you.
Luis André Blanco
CFO, Afya
Hi, Jessica. It's Blanco speaking. I will take the first one, and Virgilio going to take the second one. Regarding the first one, what we have already discussed in the last call is the pricing for this H1. We have disclosed that we've made readjustments for the medicine students that were 7.5% for these years. Within the ticket maturations, we're going to get something around 1% above that. What we delivered for the Q1 is 8.3% increase in terms of net tickets, excluding acquisitions. Just remember about our ticket dynamic. We establish our price increase annually. We usually do that in the month of September, in the beginning of October, and we establish the price for the inflations that we expect for the year. When we did that from 2021 for 2022, we did the same 7.5%.
We were behind of the inflations of 2021 because inflation speed up at the end of the year. This year of 2022, the opposite has happened. We established the same 7.5, but the inflation started to decrease at the end of the year. That's how we do that. Next September, we're going to see this inflation perspective for the year. We established a new pricing for 2024. Above these price readjustments, we have these tickets maturation effects that will come around this 1%.
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
Yeah. Just to add a point here on this question about tickets. When you take a look on table two, we also have a very high incremental on tuition when you consider also other health programs. Even excluding acquisition, the tuition fees is jumping more than 15%. That's an effect not only about price adjustment, but an effect of mix, much more concentrated in high-value programs than we had in the past. It's a good dynamic also for the year on other programs besides the medical programs for 2023. About the Mais Médicos, we are just following after the normative rule that they said that we should have to take along 120 days to release what will be the new rules for the Mais Médicos III or the new wave of capacity. It's just 60 days after they release that information.
We're expecting to have something by the end of July, beginning of August. They are working. They have their commission getting together, asking the sector, many professionals, many areas participating, how should be in addressing the new conditions for the new wave capacity, but it's still early in the process to have any information. Okay?
Jessica Mehler
Analyst, JPMorgan
Thank you. Very clear.
Renata Couto
Head of Investor Relations, Afya
We do not have other questions. Thank you so much for participating with us today. If you have any follow-up questions or if you want to schedule a call with us, just contact me and I will be pleased to help you guys. Have a good night and a great end of week. Thank you.
Virgílio Gibbon
CEO, Afya
Thank you all. Bye bye.
